units.title: Form 6 VA start: visual diary and portfolio organisation
units.intro: This unit starts Form 6 visual arts. You will continue a weekly visual diary and use a clear structure to check and organise your portfolio. Lessons teach method only and leave out school admin steps and year calendars.

lessons.title: Form 6 start: visual diary and study habits
cards: Form 6 starts by keeping the weekly visual diary, and by making the habit concrete: when you note, how much you note, and what you will ask next week.
A page can still hold a sketch, one observation, and one open question. The habit is repeating these three, not writing a long piece once.
Keep the record in class, with materials you already have.
Lessons teach method only. Note the diary gently.

quiz.question: What is the Form 6 visual-diary habit?
quiz.explain: The habit is repeating three small records each week.

quiz.question: The study habit should be ＿＿: when you note, how much, and what you ask next week.
quiz.explain: Concrete detail makes it a habit, not a slogan.

quiz.question: Match the starting habit
quiz.explain: The three together are the weekly habit.

quiz.question: Order one Form 6 diary entry.
options: Set a time to record in class
quiz.explain: Time, record, question, then next week.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, this week’s sketch; right, next week’s question.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Use “time + record + next-week question” for your Form 6 study habit. Hint: all three are possible in class, and you note them gently.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Checking and organising the portfolio
cards: Checking the portfolio means a list of what you have and what is missing: theme sentence, research evidence, a medium test, and an artwork or critical-study page.
Organising means grouping material you already have. It is not an admin form, and it is not copying a year calendar.
For one missing item, write one way to fill it, and keep that way possible in class.
Lessons teach method only and leave out school admin steps.

quiz.question: What does a portfolio check mainly look at?
options: Whether an admin form is filled
What you have and what is missing
quiz.answer: What you have and what is missing
quiz.explain: The check is a list, not an admin process.

quiz.question: Organising means you ＿＿ material you already have, not copy a calendar.
quiz.explain: Grouping shows what is missing.

quiz.question: Match the check list

answer.A gap: One classroom way to fill it

quiz.explain: Write both what you have and what is missing.

quiz.question: Order checking and organising.
options: Write one classroom way to fill it
quiz.explain: List, group, gap, then one way to fill it.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one item you have; right, one gap and how you will fill it.
options: A gap and how to fill it
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Use “two items you have + one gap + one way to fill it” to check the portfolio. Hint: the way to fill it is possible in class, and you do not write an admin step.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

units.title: Ming–Qing aesthetics and contemporary comparison
units.intro: This unit uses a compact timeline to introduce Ming–Qing aesthetics, and compares them with the Young British Artists (YBA) and related contemporary approaches. You will meet Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming. This is an introduction only, not a course in copying famous paintings one by one. Lessons do not use real exam papers.

lessons.title: Ming–Qing aesthetics and art-history intro
cards: The Ming–Qing introduction uses a compact timeline: learn a rough order, then look at form and a possible everyday use in one work.
An aesthetic question can ask: is the brushwork open or dense, is there more or less empty space, and does the work feel more private or more social?
This is an introduction only, not a course in copying famous paintings one by one.
Lessons do not use real exam papers.

quiz.question: What does the Ming–Qing timeline help you do?
options: Copy famous paintings one by one
Place one work in a rough order
Hand in a real exam paper
quiz.answer: Place one work in a rough order
quiz.explain: A compact timeline is a rough place.

quiz.question: An aesthetic question can ask whether brushwork is open or ＿＿.
quiz.explain: Open and dense is a formal comparison.

quiz.question: Match the Ming–Qing introduction

answer.Use: Whether it feels more private or more social

quiz.explain: The three items are enough for one introduction.

quiz.question: Order the Ming–Qing introduction.
options: Describe whether brushwork is open or dense
quiz.explain: Timeline, work, brushwork, then use.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, open or dense brushwork; right, one possible everyday use.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, introduce Ming–Qing aesthetics. Hint: sentence one is a rough place in time and the brushwork; sentence two is one possible use. You do not copy a whole painting.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Young British Artists (YBA) and contemporary comparison
cards: The Young British Artists (YBA) are one side of a contemporary comparison. Look at how they use material, title, and setting to talk about identity or everyday life.
The other side is the Ming–Qing observation you have started. Compare methods, such as enlarging one object, or turning the everyday into the subject.
Write the full name Young British Artists (YBA). Do not use the three letters alone as the title.
Lessons do not use real exam papers, and they do not copy exam prompts.

quiz.question: How should this group of artists be named?
quiz.explain: The full name is clear. The letters are only a note.

quiz.question: The comparison is about ＿＿, not copied exam prompts.
quiz.explain: Method is what can sit beside Ming–Qing.

quiz.question: Match the two sides

answer.Method: Enlarge an object, or make the everyday the subject

quiz.explain: Both sides are compared through method.

quiz.question: Order one contemporary comparison.
options: Write Young British Artists (YBA) in full
Choose one method of material or title
quiz.explain: Full name, method, Ming–Qing, then the comparison.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one Young British Artists (YBA) method; right, one Ming–Qing form. No copied exam prompt.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, set the Young British Artists (YBA) beside Ming–Qing work. Hint: sentence one is the full name and one method; sentence two is one Ming–Qing form. Do not copy an exam prompt.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming
cards: Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming are two artists you meet in the Ming–Qing introduction. This lesson asks for one formal note on each.
A note might cover how rocks are dotted, how dense the trees are, or how an inscription sits with the picture. Say what you see. Do not memorise a full biography.
Compare one similarity and one difference. This is an introduction only.
Lessons do not use real exam papers, and they do not copy famous paintings one by one.

quiz.question: What do you hand in for Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming?
quiz.explain: The introduction is a formal note, not a biography.

quiz.question: When comparing the two, write one similarity and one ＿＿.
quiz.explain: A comparison needs both.

quiz.question: Match formal notes

answer.Rocks: Whether the dots are dense or open
answer.Inscription: How it sits with the picture

quiz.explain: All three are forms you can see.

quiz.question: Order the introduction to Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming.
quiz.explain: Note each artist, then compare.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one form in Shen Zhou; right, one form in Wen Zhengming.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, introduce Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming. Hint: one formal note each. No full biography, and no copied painting.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

units.title: How heritage shapes everyday life
units.intro: This unit starts from how heritage shapes everyday life. You will meet Xu Wei, Chen Chun and Tang Yin, then look at symbols and identity in Bada Shanren, and at figure painting through Chen Hongshou and Wu Bin. You will use ink and mixed media to develop the first portfolio piece. Interviews and collecting stay as classroom practice.

lessons.title: How heritage shapes everyday life
cards: How heritage shapes everyday life starts from an object you use, a festival colour, or how things are arranged at home.
Write three things: the form, where it appears in a day, and which habit you think is still there.
Interviews and collecting stay as classroom practice. Use a conversation, a photo you already have, or a classroom object.
This lesson does not say that everyday life can be seen only by leaving class.

quiz.question: Where does this lesson ask you to start?
options: One everyday object or one colour
quiz.answer: One everyday object or one colour
quiz.explain: Start from a form you can see in everyday life.

quiz.question: Interviews and collecting stay as ＿＿ practice.
quiz.explain: Both stay in the classroom.

quiz.question: Match everyday influence

answer.Form: How the object or colour appears
answer.Place: Where it shows up in a day
answer.Habit: Which tradition you think is still there

quiz.explain: All three together show an influence.

quiz.question: Order one everyday observation.
options: Choose an object or a colour
Note where it appears in a day
Name one habit that is still there
quiz.explain: Object, form, place, then habit.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, the form; right, one tradition you think is still there.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In three sentences, show how heritage shapes one everyday thing for you. Hint: one sentence each for form, place, and habit, all possible in class.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Xu Wei, Chen Chun and Tang Yin
cards: Xu Wei, Chen Chun, and Tang Yin are three artists you meet in this lesson. Write one formal note on each.
A note might be about fast or slow brushwork, how open the leaves are, or whether the inscription or the picture is more prominent.
You may compare only one thing they share. An introduction does not need a full biography.
Lessons do not use real exam papers, and they do not copy paintings one by one.

quiz.question: How many formal notes does this lesson ask for Xu Wei, Chen Chun, and Tang Yin?
options: One sentence for all three is enough
quiz.explain: One form each is how you meet them.

quiz.question: An introductory comparison can name only one shared ＿＿.
quiz.explain: One shared point is enough for an introduction.

quiz.question: Match a way of looking

answer.Inscription: Whether it or the picture is more prominent

quiz.explain: Any of the three directions can be used for any of them.

quiz.question: Order the introduction to the three artists.
quiz.explain: Each artist first, then one shared point.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one artist’s brushwork; right, another artist’s leaves or inscription.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Introduce Xu Wei, Chen Chun, and Tang Yin with three short lines plus one shared point. Hint: one form each, and compare only in the last line. No biography.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Bada Shanren: symbols and identity
cards: Bada Shanren is studied here through symbols and identity: how a bird, a rock, or a signature makes you read the maker as a certain kind of person.
Write the sign as “might”. Describe the form, then suggest how it carries identity.
Identity is not a memorised life story. Name the detail in the picture that supports your suggestion.
Lessons do not use real exam papers, and they do not copy a picture.

quiz.question: What does the Bada Shanren lesson ask you to connect?
options: A full life story and a score
quiz.explain: Look at symbols and identity together.

quiz.question: Write a sign’s meaning as ＿＿, not as the only answer.
quiz.explain: “Might” keeps it a suggestion.

quiz.question: Match a Bada Shanren note

answer.Signature: A detail that might carry identity

quiz.explain: Keep the form and the suggestion apart.

quiz.question: Order one look at symbol and identity.
options: Choose a bird, a rock, or a signature
Point to the detail that supports it
quiz.explain: Form, possible identity, then the supporting detail.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, form only; right, identity with “might”.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, write about symbols and identity in Bada Shanren. Hint: sentence one is form only; sentence two uses “might” for identity and names one detail. Do not copy a picture.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Figure painting, ink, and the first portfolio piece
cards: Figure-painting introduction can look at Chen Hongshou and Wu Bin: proportion, the lines of clothing, and how an expression is exaggerated.
Ink tests still change one condition at a time. Record the effect, then decide whether it can serve a figure.
The first portfolio piece uses a structure: theme sentence, one figure-painting form, one ink or mixed-media test, and a next step.
Interviews and collecting stay as classroom practice. Lessons do not use high-score exemplars.

quiz.question: Which item belongs in the first portfolio piece?
options: A theme sentence and one medium test
quiz.answer: A theme sentence and one medium test
quiz.explain: The first piece uses theme, form, a test, and a next step.

quiz.question: Figure painting can look at proportion, clothing lines, and how an expression is ＿＿.
quiz.explain: Exaggeration is a formal method.

quiz.question: Match the first piece

answer.Next step: The figure method you want to try next

quiz.explain: The three items serve the first piece.

quiz.question: Order figure painting and the first piece.
quiz.explain: Theme, form, test, then next step.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one figure-painting form; right, one ink effect.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Use “theme sentence + figure form + one test” for the first portfolio piece. Hint: name the condition you changed. Do not use a high-score exemplar.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

units.title: Literati painting and traditional symbols
units.intro: This unit continues traditional symbol study and introduces literati painting, including the Four Monks and related schools. Practise describing form, brush and ink, and possible meanings. All of it happens in class, and it does not copy public exam questions.

lessons.title: Traditional symbols: colour, pattern and painting
cards: Traditional symbols can sit in colour, pattern, and painting. Describe the form first, then one possible meaning.
A first look at postmodern method only asks whether meaning can be completed by the viewer, and whether an object can leave its original use. You do not copy an exam prompt.
All of it happens in class. Use a classroom diagram and your own sentences.
It does not copy public exam questions.

quiz.question: When you talk about a traditional symbol, what comes first?
options: Write the only correct meaning first
Describe the form, then a possible meaning
quiz.answer: Describe the form, then a possible meaning
quiz.explain: Form first, possible meaning second.

quiz.question: A first look at method can ask whether meaning can be completed by the ＿＿.
quiz.explain: A viewer taking part in meaning is a question of method.

quiz.question: Match symbol and method

answer.A first look at method: Whether a viewer can complete the meaning

quiz.explain: All three are discussed in class, with no copied prompt.

quiz.question: Order one symbol description.
options: Point to colour, pattern, or painting
Ask whether a viewer can take part in that meaning
quiz.explain: Form, meaning, then a question of method.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, form; right, one possible meaning. Do not copy an exam prompt.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, describe one traditional symbol. Hint: sentence one is only the form of colour, pattern, or painting; sentence two uses “might” for meaning. Do not copy a public exam question.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Literati painting: the Four Monks and related schools
cards: Literati painting here includes the Four Monks and related schools. You do not rewrite them as another fixed list. Give one form and one possible meaning.
Form might be dry or wet brush and ink, empty space in the composition, or how an inscription relates to the picture.
“Related schools” means there are nearby ways of working. Compare methods. Do not memorise a complete roster.
All of it happens in class, and it does not copy public exam questions.

quiz.question: How does the literati introduction treat the Four Monks and related schools?
options: Rewrite them as another fixed list
Give one form and one possible meaning
A full roster is required to pass
quiz.answer: Give one form and one possible meaning
quiz.explain: The introduction is form and a possible meaning, not another roster.

quiz.question: Brush-and-ink looking can ask whether it is dry or ＿＿.
quiz.explain: Dry and wet is a matter of form.

quiz.question: Match the literati introduction

answer.Four Monks and related schools: Do not rewrite them as another fixed list

quiz.explain: All three happen in class.

quiz.question: Order the literati introduction.
options: Choose one form of brushwork or empty space
Say you did not rewrite the list
quiz.explain: From form to meaning, without rewriting the list.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, brush and ink or empty space; right, one possible meaning.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, introduce literati painting. Hint: sentence one is one form among the Four Monks and related schools; sentence two uses “might” for meaning. Do not rewrite them as another fixed list, and do not copy an exam prompt.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

units.title: Role-taking: re-presenting in a Chinese context
units.intro: This unit practises role-taking and re-presenting identity: how to re-present a person in a Chinese context. You may compare methods used by artists such as Cindy Sherman to discuss identity through role-play (method only, no copied exam prompts). You will also meet the Yangzhou Eccentrics, Xu Beihong and Qi Baishi, and use wet and dry media to develop the second portfolio piece.

lessons.title: Role-taking and re-presenting identity
cards: Role-taking and re-presenting identity means deciding how a person appears again: clothing, pose, setting, and the angle of looking.
Artists such as Cindy Sherman use role-play to discuss identity. This lesson is method only: which detail makes identity read as another kind of person. No copied exam prompt.
Re-presenting in a Chinese context may borrow a traditional pose or sign. Write what you changed.
Lessons do not use high-score exemplars.

quiz.question: What do you learn from artists such as Cindy Sherman here?
options: A method of discussing identity through role-play
Role-play is possible only outside class
quiz.answer: A method of discussing identity through role-play
quiz.explain: Method only, with no copied prompt.

quiz.question: After borrowing a traditional pose, write what you ＿＿.
quiz.explain: Borrowing and the change together re-present the person.

quiz.question: Match re-presenting identity

answer.Role-play: A detail that makes identity read differently

quiz.explain: All three are method.

quiz.question: Order one role-taking practice.
options: Borrow one method or traditional detail
quiz.explain: Person, presentation, borrowing, then the change.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one role-play detail; right, what you change in a Chinese context. Method only.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In two sentences, write about role-taking and re-presenting identity. Hint: sentence one is one role-play method; sentence two is what you change in a Chinese context. Do not copy an exam prompt.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Yangzhou Eccentrics, Xu Beihong and Qi Baishi
cards: The Yangzhou Eccentrics, Xu Beihong, and Qi Baishi are names you meet here. Write one formal note for each.
A note might be the subject (flowers and birds, figures, animals), dry or wet brushwork, or how much empty space is left.
Treat the Yangzhou Eccentrics as one group of methods. This lesson does not split them into another full roster.
Lessons do not use real exam papers, and they do not copy paintings one by one.

quiz.question: How are the Yangzhou Eccentrics treated in this lesson?
options: They must be split into another full roster
As one group of methods, with one formal note
Copy them into a real exam paper
quiz.answer: As one group of methods, with one formal note
quiz.explain: One formal note for the group is enough.

quiz.question: A formal note can cover subject, brushwork, or how much ＿＿ is left.
quiz.explain: Empty space is a matter of form.

quiz.question: Match the three names

answer.Yangzhou Eccentrics: Seen as one group of methods

quiz.explain: One form each completes the introduction.

quiz.question: Order the three introductions.
options: One form for the Yangzhou Eccentrics
Write one method you want to try again
quiz.explain: Three forms, then a method of your own.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one form in the Yangzhou Eccentrics; right, one form in Xu Beihong or Qi Baishi.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: In three sentences, introduce the Yangzhou Eccentrics, Xu Beihong, and Qi Baishi. Hint: one form per sentence. Do not split the Yangzhou Eccentrics into another full roster.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Wet and dry media and the second portfolio piece
cards: Dry media keep an edge more easily. Wet media spread more easily. Use that difference to develop the second portfolio piece.
The second piece is structured as: theme sentence, one identity detail, one dry or wet test, and a next step.
Each test changes one condition, and you write how it serves the person you are re-presenting.
Lessons do not use high-score student exemplars or real exam papers.

quiz.question: Which test belongs in the second portfolio piece?
options: One dry or wet medium test
quiz.answer: One dry or wet medium test
quiz.explain: The second piece uses a medium test and an identity detail.

quiz.question: Each test changes only one ＿＿.
quiz.explain: One condition shows which identity detail the effect serves.

quiz.question: Match the second piece

answer.Identity detail: The test serves the person you re-present

quiz.explain: Write the medium and the identity together.

quiz.question: Order the second piece.
options: Make one dry or wet test
quiz.explain: Theme, identity, test, then next step.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one dry or wet effect; right, how it serves an identity detail.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Use “theme sentence + identity detail + one wet-or-dry test” for the second portfolio piece. Hint: name the condition you changed. Do not use a high-score exemplar.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

units.title: Portfolio review and reflection
units.intro: This unit practises reviewing the Form 6 portfolio: looking at strengths and next steps, and writing a short overview. Lessons do not use real exam papers or high-score exemplars.

lessons.title: How to review the portfolio and next steps
cards: Review the Form 6 portfolio: which page of research is clear, and which work does not yet show the theme.
A strength needs one piece of your own evidence. The next step is one action you can do in class.
Do not turn the review into an admin handover, and do not write a year calendar.
Lessons do not use real exam papers or high-score exemplars.

quiz.question: When you review the portfolio, what must a strength include?
options: One piece of your own evidence
quiz.answer: One piece of your own evidence
quiz.explain: The evidence comes from your own portfolio.

quiz.question: The next step is one ＿＿ you can do in class.
quiz.explain: One action is enough.

quiz.question: Match the portfolio review

answer.Theme not yet shown: The sentence the work still lacks

quiz.explain: The three items make the review.

quiz.question: Order the portfolio review.
options: Name one work that does not yet show the theme
quiz.explain: Strength, evidence, a gap, then an action.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one strength and its evidence; right, one next step.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Use “strength + evidence + next step” to review the Form 6 portfolio. Hint: do not write an admin step, and do not use a real exam paper or a high-score exemplar.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

lessons.title: Structure for a portfolio overview
cards: A portfolio overview uses four moves: one theme sentence, what the research workbook did, what the artwork or critical study shows, and the next step.
The two parts support each other. The overview can say which workbook page matches which decision in the work.
This lesson does not lock a word count. Each of the four sentences does one job.
Lessons do not use real exam papers or high-score exemplars.

quiz.question: Which part must the overview mention?
options: The research workbook and the artwork or critical study
quiz.answer: The research workbook and the artwork or critical study
quiz.explain: The overview joins the workbook and the work.

quiz.question: The overview says which workbook page matches which ＿＿ in the work.
quiz.explain: The page and the decision support each other.

quiz.question: Match the overview
quiz.explain: Add the next step and the four moves are complete.

quiz.question: Order the portfolio overview.
options: What the artwork or critical study shows
quiz.explain: Theme, workbook, work, then next step.

quiz.question: Compare works: left, one workbook page; right, one decision in the work. Say how they match.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper

quiz.question: Write a portfolio overview in four sentences. Hint: one each for theme, workbook, artwork or critical study, and next step. There is no word-count lock, and you do not use a real exam paper or a high-score exemplar.
quiz.explain: Practice structure · lessons do not use a real exam paper
